units.title: Unit 1: Cells, Organelles & Human Body Systems

lessons.title: Cell Theory & Organelles (Part 1 of 2)
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Cell Parts and Functions
lessons.reading: All living things are made of cells. The nucleus holds DNA, mitochondria release energy, and the cell membrane controls what enters and exits. Plant cells also have chloroplasts for sunlight and a stiff cell wall.

principles.title: Cell Organelles and Plant vs. Animal Cells
principles.summary: Identify the jobs of the nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplasts, cell wall, and membrane.

bank.prompt: Which organelle makes usable energy (ATP) for the cell?
bank.explanation: Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell. They break down sugar to release usable energy.

bank.prompt: Which two structures are found in plant cells only?
bank.explanation: Plant cells have chloroplasts to capture sunlight and a stiff cell wall for support.

bank.prompt: What is the main job of the cell membrane?
choices: Control what enters and leaves the cell
bank.answer: Control what enters and leaves the cell
bank.explanation: The cell membrane is a selective barrier that lets water and nutrients in while keeping waste out.

bank.prompt: Where is DNA stored inside a plant or animal cell?
bank.explanation: The nucleus is the control center of a eukaryotic cell and holds the DNA.

bank.prompt: What does modern Cell Theory state about all living things?
choices: All living things are made of cells
Only animals are made of cells
New cells form from nonliving dust
Every cell is visible without a microscope
bank.answer: All living things are made of cells
bank.explanation: Cell theory states that all living things are made of cells, and cells come from existing cells.

bank.prompt: Which organelle captures sunlight to make sugar in plants?
bank.explanation: Chloroplasts contain green chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis to make sugar from sunlight.

bank.prompt: Why do plant cells have a large central vacuole?
choices: To store water and keep stems upright
bank.answer: To store water and keep stems upright
bank.explanation: A full central vacuole pushes against the cell wall so the plant stands tall instead of wilting.

bank.prompt: What is the jelly-like fluid that fills a cell?
bank.explanation: Cytoplasm is the jelly-like fluid inside the cell membrane that holds the organelles in place.

lessons.title: Tissues, Organs & Body Systems (Part 2 of 2)
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Organization in the Human Body
lessons.reading: Cells group into tissues, tissues form organs (like the heart and lungs), and organs team up in organ systems. Body systems work together to keep internal conditions stable (homeostasis).

principles.title: Levels of Organization and Interacting Body Systems
principles.summary: Order cell → tissue → organ → system and explain how systems cooperate.

bank.prompt: What is the correct order from simplest to most complex?
bank.explanation: Similar cells form a tissue, tissues form an organ, and organs work together in an organ system.

bank.prompt: How do the lungs and heart work together?
choices: Lungs bring in oxygen; blood carries it
Lungs pump blood; heart breathes air
They never interact inside the body
bank.answer: Lungs bring in oxygen; blood carries it
bank.explanation: The respiratory system takes in oxygen, and the circulatory system pumps that oxygen to body cells.

bank.prompt: What is a group of similar cells working together called?
bank.explanation: A tissue is a group of similar cells that perform a shared job, such as muscle tissue.

bank.prompt: Which body system breaks food down into nutrients?
bank.explanation: The digestive system breaks food into small nutrient molecules that the blood can absorb.

bank.prompt: Which two systems work together to move your arm?
bank.explanation: Muscles pull on bones at joints so the muscular and skeletal systems produce body movement.

bank.prompt: Which organ system sends electrical signals from the brain?
bank.explanation: The nervous system uses the brain, spinal cord, and nerves to send fast messages through the body.

bank.prompt: What is the heart classified as in biological organization?
bank.explanation: An organ is a structure made of different tissues working together, such as the heart or stomach.

bank.prompt: What does homeostasis mean in a living organism?
bank.explanation: Homeostasis is the maintenance of stable internal conditions, like body temperature and water balance.

units.title: Unit 2: Plate Tectonics, Ohio Rocks/Minerals & Thermal Energy

lessons.title: Plate Tectonics & Mantle Convection (Part 1 of 3)
lessons.reading: Convection currents in the hot mantle slowly move Earth’s plates. Plates pull apart at divergent boundaries, collide at convergent boundaries, and slide sideways at transform boundaries.

principles.title: Tectonic Plate Boundaries and Mantle Convection
principles.summary: Distinguish convergent, divergent, and transform plate boundaries.

bank.prompt: What force inside Earth moves tectonic plates?
bank.explanation: Hot rock rises and cooler rock sinks in the mantle. These convection currents slowly move tectonic plates.

bank.prompt: What forms when two oceanic plates pull apart?
bank.explanation: At a divergent boundary underwater, plates separate and magma rises to form a mid-ocean ridge.

bank.prompt: Which plate boundary built the Himalayan Mountains?
bank.explanation: At a convergent boundary, two continental plates collide and push crust upward into mountains.

bank.prompt: How do plates move at the San Andreas Fault?
choices: They slide horizontally past each other
bank.answer: They slide horizontally past each other
bank.explanation: At a transform boundary, two plates grind sideways past each other and cause frequent earthquakes.

bank.prompt: What evidence supported Wegener’s Continental Drift idea?
choices: Matching coastlines and matching fossils across oceans
Warm ocean water at the equator
bank.answer: Matching coastlines and matching fossils across oceans
bank.explanation: Continental drift is supported by puzzle-fit coastlines and identical fossils found on separate continents.

bank.prompt: What happens during subduction at a plate boundary?
choices: A dense oceanic plate sinks into the mantle
Rivers drop sand at a delta
Two clouds collide in a storm
bank.answer: A dense oceanic plate sinks into the mantle
bank.explanation: Subduction occurs when a denser oceanic plate slides beneath a lighter plate into the mantle.

bank.prompt: Which layer of Earth is broken into tectonic plates?
bank.explanation: The lithosphere is Earth’s rigid outer shell of crust and upper mantle broken into plates.

bank.prompt: Why does the Pacific Ring of Fire have many volcanoes?
choices: It sits along active subduction zones
The equator heats the Pacific floor
bank.answer: It sits along active subduction zones
bank.explanation: Subduction zones around the Pacific Plate melt rock into magma, creating volcanoes and earthquakes.

lessons.title: Ohio Earth Science: Minerals, Rock Cycle & Soil (Part 2 of 3)
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: The Rock Cycle & Minerals (OH.6.ESS.1-4)
lessons.reading: Minerals are identified by properties like hardness and streak. Igneous rock cools from magma, sedimentary rock (like Ohio limestone) compacts from layers of sediment, and metamorphic rock changes under heat and pressure.

principles.title: Minerals, Igneous/Sedimentary/Metamorphic Rocks & Soil
principles.summary: Classify igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks, mineral hardness, and soil humus.

bank.prompt: How do igneous rocks form?
choices: Cooling and hardening of magma or lava
Gluing sand grains under ocean water
bank.answer: Cooling and hardening of magma or lava
bank.explanation: Igneous rock forms when melted rock (magma underground or lava on the surface) cools and solidifies.

bank.prompt: How do sedimentary rocks like Ohio limestone form?
choices: Layers of sediment compact and cement together
Pure iron melts in the core
bank.answer: Layers of sediment compact and cement together
bank.explanation: Sedimentary rock forms when layers of sediment or shells are pressed and cemented together over time.

bank.prompt: What turns existing rock into metamorphic rock?
choices: Intense heat and pressure without melting
bank.answer: Intense heat and pressure without melting
bank.explanation: Metamorphic rock forms deep underground when heat and pressure change a rock’s structure without melting it.

bank.prompt: Which mineral property is tested using the Mohs scale?
bank.explanation: The Mohs hardness scale ranks minerals from 1 (talc) to 10 (diamond) by scratch resistance.

bank.prompt: What does a mineral’s streak test show?
choices: The color of its powdered form
bank.answer: The color of its powdered form
bank.explanation: Streak is the color of a mineral’s powder left on an unglazed porcelain plate.

bank.prompt: Why do intrusive igneous rocks have large crystals?
choices: Lava cools instantly in cold water
bank.explanation: Slow cooling underground gives mineral crystals plenty of time to grow large, as in granite.

bank.prompt: Which rock type most often contains ancient fossils?
bank.explanation: Sedimentary rock forms in layers at cooler surface temperatures that preserve shells and bones as fossils.

bank.prompt: What is humus in topsoil?
choices: Decayed organic matter from plants and animals
Pure salt crystals from the sea
bank.answer: Decayed organic matter from plants and animals
bank.explanation: Humus is dark, nutrient-rich organic material formed from decomposed leaves and organisms in soil.

lessons.title: Thermal Energy Transfer & Water Cycle (Part 3 of 3)
lessons.reading: Heat flows from warmer to cooler objects by conduction (touch), convection (fluid circulation), and radiation (waves through space). Sunlight and gravity power the global water cycle.

principles.title: Conduction, Convection, Radiation & Water Cycle Drivers
principles.summary: Identify conduction, convection, radiation, and water cycle forces.

bank.prompt: A spoon in hot soup gets warm by which process?
bank.explanation: Conduction is heat transfer through direct contact between touching particles in a solid.

bank.prompt: How does heat from the Sun travel through space?
bank.explanation: Radiation transfers energy as electromagnetic waves that can travel across empty space.

bank.prompt: Warm water rises and cool water sinks by which process?
bank.explanation: Convection transfers heat by the circulation of warm, less-dense fluid rising and cool fluid sinking.

bank.prompt: What two forces drive Earth’s global water cycle?
bank.explanation: Sunlight powers evaporation into the air, and gravity pulls rain and river runoff back down.

bank.prompt: Which way does thermal energy naturally flow?
choices: From warmer objects to cooler objects
From cooler objects to warmer objects
bank.answer: From warmer objects to cooler objects
bank.explanation: Thermal energy always flows from a higher-temperature object to a lower-temperature object.

bank.prompt: Why do winter coats trap pockets of air?
choices: Trapped air is a thermal insulator
Air makes the coat conduct heat faster
bank.answer: Trapped air is a thermal insulator
bank.explanation: A thermal insulator slows down heat transfer so your body warmth stays inside the coat.

bank.prompt: What happens when water vapor cools high in the sky?
choices: It condenses into liquid cloud droplets
It disappears from the water cycle
bank.answer: It condenses into liquid cloud droplets
bank.explanation: Condensation is the change of water vapor gas into liquid droplets when air cools.

bank.prompt: Which material is the best thermal conductor for a pan?
bank.explanation: Metals like copper and aluminum are thermal conductors that let heat pass through quickly.

remediation.workedExample: Example: "What force inside Earth moves tectonic plates?" → Answer: Convection currents in the mantle. (Hot rock rises and cooler rock sinks in the mantle. These convection currents slowly move tectonic plates.)
